name: recyclebin_i
description: Parse $Recycle.Bin $I metadata (version 1 and 2 records, unsigned fields): the original path, original size and deletion time (raw FILETIME and ISO 8601 UTC with seven fractional digits), for one file or every $I under a directory in sorted order. Every length is checked against the bytes the file has: a record shorter than its layout needs is reported truncated with the bytes it has and the path decoded from them as far as it goes, never as a complete one; a longer one carries trailing_bytes; a file over 1 MiB is not read (it is not a $I); an unknown header is not guessed at. Every candidate is checked as it is found and opened without blocking and without following a link: a $I that is a link, a FIFO, a device, a socket or a directory is not opened and is counted in not_attempted (each with its entry and the reason, status partial), a directory that cannot be listed is an entry too, and a link to a directory is not followed (a path that is itself a link to a directory is refused). Nothing here can hang on a FIFO or lose the rest of the bin. The whole record is read, not a fixed 4096 bytes. Each entry names its $R counterpart where present and the SID of the bin directory it sits in. The bin's SID is the account whose bin received the item; it does not say who deleted the file or from where. The tool has its own clock (54 s of the manifest's 60): when it runs out the sweep stops, the pages written so far are placed and named, and the answer is partial with a status_basis that says where it stopped and how many names were walked and $I files read; every answer carries status and status_basis (complete only for an input read to its end), a wrong-type argument is refused as JSON (status failed), and SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with one JSON document (status failed with interrupted true, exit 128 plus the signal) and no temporary file. A result file is never replaced: the same result keeps its name, another takes the next free -n name. The directory walk is inside the clock too.

path.description: A $I file, or a directory holding them

limit.description: Entries shown inline (default 500, 1 to 10000, an inline page size); every $I file is read, and when more match the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results
